claims.claim: Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis, Palestine, after 310 and died in 403.
Epiphanius was elected bishop of Constantia (Salamis) in 367 and served for nearly forty years.
On the Twelve Gems (De duodecim gemmis / De xii gemmis) was written at the request of Diodorus, bishop of Tyre.
The work is an exegetical treatise on the twelve gemstones on the High Priest's breastplate (Exodus 28:17–20 and 39:10–13).
It is the oldest Christian book on gemstones.
Epiphanius deals with the stones according to their appearance, their healing powers, and their attribution to the twelve tribes from a Christian point of view.
Only extracts of the work are preserved in Greek.
Other surviving versions include parts of a Latin translation, parts of an Armenian version, Coptic fragments, an extract in Syriac, and tradition in Arabic.
The Georgian translation is important for Georgian philology as one of the earliest and most valuable extant monuments of that language.
The Latin version contains barely one half of the original document.
